title: The Two Plastic Bags and the Mountain: Patagonia, Patagon, and the Vault Under Uri
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Ranch and the Two Plastic Bags

stops.name: Gobernador Costa, the birth the record cannot fix
stops.date_confidence: Date attested three independent ways: the en.wikipedia infobox reads '26 February 1974'; PayPal's 2016 DEF 14A gives 'Age 42'; Pagina/12 of 1 August 1999 calls him 25. Place is reconstruction and disputed. En.wikipedia's infobox gives Gobernador Costa, Chubut; Infobae and Diario Jornada both print Esquel (next stop). No civil registry entry or birth certificate was located for either town. The coordinate is the es.wikipedia infobox figure for Gobernador Costa, 44 deg 04 min S, 70 deg 35 min O.
stops.campa: He is born on the twenty-sixth of February, eldest of four children in a sheep-ranching family of the Chubut steppe. Most biographies put the house at Gobernador Costa, a road town between the cordillera and the dry plateau where wool is trucked out and everything else is trucked in. The date is fixed three ways: an encyclopedia infobox, a Buenos Aires interviewer counting his years aloud, and a proxy statement filed with the American securities regulator by a payments company that will one day seat him on its board. For the town there is no registry entry, only repetition.
suggested_refs: The competing birthplace at Esquel, Chubut, next stop

stops.name: Esquel, the other town
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction, and the direct competitor to the previous stop. Two Argentine outlets fetched independently give Esquel verbatim: Infobae, 22 April 2018, 'Nacio hace 44 anos en Esquel, Chubut, Patagonia, Argentina', and Diario Jornada in the same wording. Neither cites a civil record. Some profiles hedge further and say only 'in a field near Esquel'. Both towns are kept on the map because the sources are irreconcilable, not because he was born twice.
stops.campa: A hundred and thirty kilometres north, at the foot of the Andes, sits the other town the record offers. Two Argentine newspapers state flatly that he was born in Esquel, in the same words, four years apart. Others hedge and say a field near Esquel. Nobody produces a certificate. The family ranch itself has no name in any consulted source, no acreage, no cadastral number; it is present in every biography and absent from every register. Both towns stay on the map because the two accounts cannot be reconciled.
suggested_refs: Infobae, Muriel Balbi interview, 22 April 2018
sources: infobae.com, 'Exitoso y visionario: como es y como piensa Wenceslao Casares', 22 April 2018 (fetched)

stops.name: The estancia in Chubut, four children and the tension
stops.date_confidence: Placeholder coordinate for an unnamed and unlocated ranch, disclosed as such: no estancia name, extent or location appears in any source consulted, so the pin is a mid-Chubut approximation between the two candidate birth towns. The date orders the segment and is not attested; the recollections are retrospective, given in the Infobae interview of 22 April 2018 and the Unchained interview of February 2018, and describe the 1970s and 1980s from a distance of thirty years.
stops.campa: The ranch runs sheep and the family runs on wool prices, which in this country are set by decisions made a thousand kilometres north. Devaluation, inflation, the periodic national wreck: the boy does not follow the mechanics, he watches his parents' faces. He is the eldest of four. He will say later that what he suffered was not the loss of money but the sight of what the loss did to the adults, and that the household lost everything three separate times, each time because of something a government or a bank had done.
stops.quote: Cuando era chico sufri mucho ver lo que le pasaba a mis padres debido a las cosas que pasaban en la Argentina con la devaluacion, inflacion y todos esos 'despelotes' que hubo en el pais.
stops.quote_source: Infobae, interview by Muriel Balbi, 22 April 2018 (accents stripped for file encoding; original carries them)
suggested_refs: Unchained podcast transcript, Laura Shin interview, 6 February 2018
sources: econtalk.org, 'Wences Casares on Bitcoin and Xapo', 20 July 2015 (fetched)

stops.name: Chubut, the supermarket and the man with the price gun
stops.date_confidence: The hyperinflation of 1989 is public record; the scene is self-reported, given once, in the Unchained interview of February 2018, and corroborated by no second witness. Month is chosen to sit inside the worst of the 1989 spiral and orders the segment only. Same placeholder ranch-area coordinate as the previous stop. Note a discrepancy left standing: the same account says 'me and my two sisters', which does not sit easily with the four-children figure carried elsewhere.
stops.campa: He is fifteen the year prices move faster than a shopkeeper can write them. His mother comes to the school in the middle of the morning, which she has never done, carrying two plastic bags of cash: her salary, whole, in paper that is losing value while she holds it. She hands each child an aisle and a list. They meet at the cashier, and when money is left over she sends them back for more goods, because money left over is money lost. One employee's entire job that day is to walk the aisles changing the prices.
stops.quote: I remember my mom came to take us out of school in the middle of the morning. She'd never done that before, me and my two sisters. And she was carrying two plastic bags full of cash.
stops.quote_source: Unchained podcast, Laura Shin interview with Wences Casares, February 2018 (podscripts.co transcript)
suggested_refs: The corrected second half of the same anecdote: 'And our job was to go in front of that person', per the official unchainedcrypto.com transcript
sources: unchainedcrypto.com transcript of the same interview (fetched)

stops.name: Washington, Pennsylvania, the exchange year
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The Rotary exchange year at about seventeen in Washington, Pennsylvania appears in the en.wikipedia article and in speaker-bureau and profile pages, all of them tracing back to his own retelling. No Rotary district record, host family, or school name was located. The year 1991 is inferred from a February 1974 birth and 'about seventeen'; September is the American school year's start and orders the stop.
stops.campa: A Rotary exchange places him for a year in a small city in western Pennsylvania, coal and steel country going quiet. He is seventeen. Which school took him, and which family housed him, no source reached says, and no Rotary district record has been found either. He will describe the year afterwards as the one that changed his life, and what he takes from it is not the language or the schooling but a working assumption he had not met before, that the people around him behaved as though nothing were impossible.
suggested_refs: en.wikipedia.org, 'Wences Casares'
sources: allamericanspeakers.com and stvp.stanford.edu profile pages (promotional biographies, tagged R)

segments.name: Victoria, and the Wires into Argentina

stops.name: Universidad de San Andres, Victoria, the degree that may not exist
stops.date_confidence: Contradiction left standing rather than resolved. El Cronista's retrospective 'Lo que dejo Patagon' calls Casares and Constancio Larguia graduates of San Andres; the more widely repeated account, consistent with the 1994 Internet Argentina chronology, has him leaving after about three years without finishing. Neither a diploma nor a registrar record was reached. March is the start of the Argentine academic year and orders the stop; the year is inferred from the birth date.
stops.campa: The campus sits at Vito Dumas 284 in Victoria, out along the river north of the capital, a private university barely a few years old teaching business and economics to the children of people who can pay for it. He studies here. He also meets Constancio Larguia here, and one further classmate whose identity the sources cannot agree on. Whether he graduated is a question two respectable outlets answer differently. El Cronista calls him and Larguia graduates of the place; the more widely repeated account has him leaving after about three years with nothing signed.
suggested_refs: El Cronista, 'Lo que dejo Patagon'
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'Universidad de San Andres' (coordinates, Vito Dumas 284)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Internet Argentina S.A.
stops.date_confidence: Attested in multiple business profiles and in the academic study Historia de la industria informatica argentina; month and day are unknown and defaulted. The frequent claim that this was literally Argentina's first internet service provider is not supported by any regulator's chronology reached here, so the stop says pioneering and not first. City-centroid coordinate; no office address was located.
stops.campa: He is twenty when he starts an internet service provider in a country where almost nobody has a modem. He is at this point either an undergraduate or a dropout, depending on which account is read. Internet Argentina S.A. sells access to a network most of its potential customers have not heard of, to the few offices and households that already own the equipment to reach it. It is one of the first commercial providers in the country. The claim that it was the very first survives on repetition, and no regulator's chronology reached in this research supports it.
suggested_refs: Historia de la industria informatica argentina, eitellauria.ar PDF

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Patagon and the sold bicycle
stops.date_confidence: Attested as to founding and founders' names; disputed as to capital and as to the third founder. Early money is reported variously as under US$10,000 and about US$30,000, from friends and family. Larguia's sold bicycle is his own line to Expansion, 14 September 2011. On the third founder the sources split: es.wikipedia names Federico Agardy alongside Casares and Larguia; Pagina/12 of 1 August 1999 instead names Anibal Borra, a founder and programmer by then living in Sao Paulo. Left unresolved.
stops.campa: Patagon begins as an online financial-information site and becomes a brokerage: quotes, accounts, trades, for a middle class that has never been inside a broker's office. The founding capital is small enough that the sources disagree about which small figure it was, and one of the founders funds his share by selling his bicycle. Casares and Constancio Larguia are agreed on in every account. The third name is not: one encyclopedia says Federico Agardy, and the contemporaneous Pagina/12 profile says Anibal Borra, the programmer, writing from Sao Paulo.
suggested_refs: Expansion (Mexico), 'Hasta vendi mi bicicleta', 14 September 2011

stops.name: Buenos Aires, fifty-one percent for two hundred thousand dollars
stops.date_confidence: Correction applied against widely repeated figures. Pagina/12 of 1 August 1999, contemporaneous and fetched, reports that Zsolt Agardy, a businessman of Hungarian origin who owned Editorial Estrada and the brokerage InvestCapital, put 200 mil dolares into Patagon in exchange for 51 per cent. A frequently repeated academic account instead gives about US$1 million bringing the company to full operation by mid-1998. The two are not reconcilable, and the contemporaneous figure is preferred here. Month and day unknown.
stops.campa: The money that makes Patagon a working company arrives from Zsolt Agardy, a Hungarian-born businessman in Buenos Aires who owns a schoolbook publisher and a brokerage house. What he pays is two hundred thousand dollars. What he receives is fifty-one per cent. The founders, a year and a half out of a bicycle sale, have sold control of the company before any foreign bank has heard its name. A later academic account puts the investment at about a million dollars and calls it the money that brought Patagon to full operation. The two figures cannot both be right.
suggested_refs: Pagina/12 profile of Patagon, 1 August 1999
sources: Historia de la industria informatica argentina (competing US$1 million figure, tagged R)

segments.name: What a Bank Pays for a Website

stops.name: Madrid, Santander takes three quarters
stops.date_confidence: Attested from the primary corporate announcement: Banco Santander Central Hispano's RNS of 9 March 2000, fetched at investegate.co.uk. Contradiction on the money left standing: the RNS headline values Patagon at US$705 million, while El Pais of 10 March 2000 gives the consideration as 91.5 billion pesetas, roughly US$528 million for the 75 per cent. The Open Bank integration, with Angel Corcostegui as chairman and Casares as managing director, is announced on 22 March and is folded into this stop.
stops.campa: Thirteen days before the Nasdaq peaks, a Spanish bank buys three quarters of a three-year-old Argentine website. Santander pays out Chase Capital Partners, JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs, values Patagon at seven hundred and five million dollars, and calls the purchase the first step of a new global strategy. The founding group keeps the balance. Two weeks later Patagon is folded into Open Bank under Angel Corcostegui, with Casares, twenty-six, as managing director of the combined operation.
stops.quote: the first step of a new global strategy for telecommunications and Internet business
stops.quote_source: Banco Santander Central Hispano, RNS announcement, 9 March 2000
suggested_refs: El Pais, 10 March 2000, giving the consideration as 91.5 billion pesetas

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the paper millionaire with no car
stops.date_confidence: Attested as to his statements: La Nacion, 'Es cierto que los yetties de Internet son millonarios?', quotes him saying he sold not a single share in the Santander transaction, remained a paper millionaire, lived on a monthly salary of US$6,000 and had not yet been able to buy a car. The article is dated 2000 without a fetched day, so June is a placeholder ordering the stop after the March announcement. Whether the salary figure was complete is not independently checkable.
stops.campa: The headline says a company valued at seven hundred and five million dollars. The founder tells a Buenos Aires newspaper that he has sold no shares, holds paper, draws six thousand dollars a month, and has not yet managed to buy himself a car. Both statements are true at once. Twenty-five years of profiles will collapse the two into one and report that he sold Patagon for seven hundred and fifty million dollars. The article that carries the salary figure is trying to work out whether Argentina's internet boys are actually rich, and it prints the missing car without comment.
suggested_refs: lanacion.com.ar/lifestyle/es-cierto-que-los-yetties-de-internet-son-millonarios-nid213416

stops.name: Allston, the owner-president program
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. That he attended Harvard Business School's Owner/President Management executive-education program, and met the Chilean industrialist Pablo Bosch there, comes from biographical profiles of the Las Majadas partnership; no HBS record was reached and the exact program dates are not established. This is executive education and not a Harvard degree. Coordinate corrected to the HBS Allston campus, 42.3672, -71.1225, per the en.wikipedia infobox; a figure four kilometres south had reached this file.
stops.campa: Across the Charles from Cambridge, in the brick quadrangle Harvard keeps on the Allston side, the business school runs a program for people who already own companies. He comes as the managing director of a bank subsidiary he did not intend to be working for, and here he meets a Chilean industrialist named Pablo Bosch, who will be his partner in a Chilean house for the next twenty years. The program itself is executive education: three short residencies spread over several years, and no degree at the end of it.
stops.quote: Yo no puedo cambiar cuan inteligente soy... Pero si tengo mucho control sobre cuan perseverante puedo ser. Y creo que muchas veces la diferencia entre exito y fracaso es la perseverancia.
stops.quote_source: Infobae, interview by Muriel Balbi, 22 April 2018 (accents stripped for file encoding)
suggested_refs: Pablo Bosch, later co-owner of Las Majadas de Pirque
sources: Secondary biographical profiles of the Las Majadas partnership (tagged R)

stops.name: Madrid, six hundred sixteen million written off
stops.date_confidence: Attested from primary filings: Santander's RNS disposal announcement of 24 May 2002, fetched at investegate.co.uk, and the corresponding CNMV filing. The bank buys the outstanding 11.41 per cent of Patagon Euro S.L. from Casares, Guillermo Kirchner and other minority holders for US$22.02 million, sells Patagon America to Casares and Kirchner for US$9.84 million, and requires the Patagon brand out of the American entity within thirty days.
stops.campa: Two years and two months after buying it, Santander charges seven hundred million euros against its second quarter, of which six hundred and sixteen million is goodwill it will never amortise. He will later call the original sale a mistake, meaning that he stopped building a company in order to be bought. The bank takes full ownership of the European holding company from the founders for twenty-two million dollars and sells the American business back to Casares and Guillermo Kirchner for nine point eight four, on the condition that the Patagon name is off it within thirty days.
suggested_refs: CNMV filing corresponding to the 24 May 2002 disposal
sources: cnmv.es filing for the Patagon disposal

segments.name: Games in Santiago, a Bank in Brazil

stops.name: Miami, the marriage
stops.date_confidence: Attested from the family's own chronology at simpaticasail.com/about-us, fetched directly, which gives the year, the city, and that they met through Endeavor, where Belle Wylie Holahan worked. Month and day are not given and default to 01. City-centroid coordinate; no venue is named.
stops.campa: He marries Belle Wylie Holahan in Miami. They met through Endeavor, the nonprofit that finds and backs entrepreneurs in countries where venture capital does not reach, and where she worked; it is the same institution that will keep putting him on stages in Buenos Aires for the next twenty years. The whole public record of the marriage is a single line on a sailing website's About page, written years afterwards, as the first item in a chronology that is mostly about a boat. It gives the year and the city and nothing else.
suggested_refs: simpaticasail.com/about-us, the family's own voyage chronology

stops.name: Santiago, Wanako Games
stops.date_confidence: Founders attested: Esteban Sosnik, Tiburcio de la Carcova, Santiago Bilinkis and Casares, per the Wikipedia article on the studio and GamesBeat coverage. Founding year 2002 is consistently reported; month unknown and chosen to order the stop after the marriage. Titles named are attested to the studio, not to Casares personally, whose day-to-day role in it is not documented in any primary source reached.
stops.campa: A video game studio in Santiago, founded by four Argentines with Chilean partners, making console titles for American publishers: Assault Heroes, 3D Ultra MiniGolf Adventures, work-for-hire under Sierra. It sits in his record between an online bank in Madrid and a correspondent bank in Brazil, and no source reached documents what he did there day to day. The studio employs Chilean programmers writing code for export at a time when the country's exports come out of the ground. The other three founders are Esteban Sosnik, Tiburcio de la Carcova and Santiago Bilinkis.
suggested_refs: gamesbeat.com, 'Chilean startup focuses on games for social good'

stops.name: Sao Paulo, Banco Lemon and the shopkeepers' counters
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction throughout. No incorporation record for Banco Lemon and no Banco do Brasil transaction announcement were located. The founding is credited across retrospective fintech profiles to Casares with Meyer 'Micky' Malka; the 2009 acquisition by Banco do Brasil of the correspondent network is likewise reported without a public price, and the legal perimeter of that sale, whole bank or network only, is unresolved. Month arbitrary; the Sao Paulo pin stands for a Brazil-wide network with no single address.
stops.campa: Banco Lemon does not build branches. It signs up the shops people already walk into, pharmacies and grocers and lottery agents, and pays them to handle deposits, withdrawals and bill payments across a country where tens of millions have no account. The counter is the branch. He builds it with Meyer Malka, who will be his partner in the next two companies as well. In 2009 Banco do Brasil buys the correspondent network; nobody has ever published what it paid.
stops.quote: Hacer con los servicios financieros lo que hizo WhatsApp con las comunicaciones. Eso me motiva muchisimo.
stops.quote_source: Infobae, interview by Muriel Balbi, 22 April 2018 (accents stripped for file encoding)
suggested_refs: Meyer 'Micky' Malka, co-founder here and at Bling Nation
sources: Retrospective fintech-industry profiles of Casares's ventures (tagged R)

stops.name: Miami, the lines untied
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the family's own chronology at simpaticasail.com/about-us: they sail days after Diogenes's first birthday and finish in Miami in February 2007, 'almost three years after departing', which puts departure in mid-2004. Correction carried: a birth year of 2004 for Diogenes had reached this file and is arithmetically impossible against those two statements; he is born in 2003. Month is inferred from the three-year span, not stated.
stops.campa: The catamaran is called Simpatica. The plan is to sail around the world with a one-year-old aboard, and the departure has already been postponed more than once, because there is always another item left on the checklist. On the day finally set for leaving he wants one more week. His own father is standing on the dock. He does not argue the point; he bends down and starts working the lines off the cleats while his son is still talking, and there is a short exchange in Spanish while he does it.
stops.quote: En eso, mi papa empieza a deshacer los cabos. Yo le dije 'Papa! No!'. El contesto: 'Te vas ahora'.
stops.quote_source: Infobae, interview by Muriel Balbi, 22 April 2018 (accents and inverted punctuation stripped for file encoding)
suggested_refs: simpaticasail.com/about-us

stops.name: Nuku Hiva, a third of the way
stops.date_confidence: The route is attested at simpaticasail.com/about-us, which itemises the Marquesas, the Tuamotus, Tahiti, Moorea and Bora Bora but gives no call dates for any island. The date here orders the leg between a mid-2004 departure and a mid-2005 birth in Auckland and is not documented. Nuku Hiva is the standard Marquesan landfall for a Pacific crossing and stands for the group.
stops.campa: The Pacific crossing is the long one: weeks with no land in any direction, a small child aboard, two adults standing watches around the clock. They come in through the Marquesas, where the volcanic cliffs drop straight into deep water, and work west through the Tuamotus to Tahiti, Moorea, Bora Bora. The family website that records all of this lists the islands in a row and dates not one of them. By the time the atolls are behind them the boat has covered roughly a third of the circumference of the earth.
suggested_refs: simpaticasail.com/about-us

stops.name: Auckland, the little Kiwi
stops.date_confidence: Attested at simpaticasail.com/about-us: Theodore Casares is born in Auckland one year into the voyage and is nicknamed the little Kiwi. The site gives neither month nor day; June is derived from 'one year into' a mid-2004 departure and orders the stop only.
stops.campa: A year out from Miami the boat stops in New Zealand long enough for the second son to be born ashore, in a city with hospitals, in a country neither parent is from. They call him Theodore. He acquires a New Zealand birthplace, a nickname, and a berth on a boat that is going to keep going west. The family's own chronology gives the nickname, the little Kiwi, and then moves straight on to Indonesia without another word about the stop. There are now two children under three living aboard a catamaran in the South Pacific.
suggested_refs: simpaticasail.com/about-us

stops.name: Bali, west with two children aboard
stops.date_confidence: Route attested at simpaticasail.com/about-us: Bali, Kupang, Riung and Alor, then Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand, and onward through Sri Lanka, Oman, India, Egypt and Israel toward the Suez Canal. No dates are given for any call. The date here orders the leg between the Auckland birth and the February 2007 finish. Bali stands for the whole Indian Ocean passage.
stops.campa: Indonesia, then the Malacca strait, then Thailand: Bali, Kupang, Riung, Alor, Singapore. He will describe the voyage afterwards as the hardest thing he has ever undertaken, and he says it having already built and lost two companies. Beyond Thailand the route runs Sri Lanka, Oman, India, Egypt and Israel, and up through the Suez Canal into the Mediterranean for the last leg home. Two small children are aboard for all of it, with no crew but their parents, and the family's own chronology gives no date for any call between the year they left and the month they came back.
suggested_refs: simpaticasail.com/about-us

stops.name: Pirque, the palace bought by satellite phone
stops.date_confidence: Attested to lasmajadas.cl, fetched: 'En 2006, el empresario argentino Wenceslao Casares compra Las Majadas' from the Nieto family. The house was designed by Alberto Cruz Montt in 1905 with a park by Guillermo Renner, and had belonged to the Subercaseaux family before passing to the Nietos in 1928. A date of 1906 for the purchase had reached this file and is a straight data error, corrected here. The page states no price; the widely repeated figure of about US$2 million is uncorroborated. That he assessed the property by satellite phone from the boat is reported, not documented. Month arbitrary.
stops.campa: In the Maipo valley south of Santiago stands a house built in 1905 for the Subercaseaux family by Alberto Cruz Montt, with a park laid out by Guillermo Renner, sold to the Nietos in 1928 and by 2006 needing everything. He buys it. By the account that circulates he is mid-ocean at the time and does the assessment over a satellite phone with Pablo Bosch walking the rooms at the other end. The intention is a family house. No source gives what he paid.
suggested_refs: lasmajadas.cl, 'La apuesta de Pablo Bosch y Wenceslao Casares en Las Majadas de Pirque'

stops.name: Miami, the circumnavigation closed
stops.date_confidence: Attested at simpaticasail.com/about-us: 'They finished their circumnavigation in Miami in February 2007, almost three years after departing.' The same page places the family in Woodside, California afterwards and expecting a third child. Day not given.
stops.campa: They come back into Miami in February, almost three years out. The boat left from this same coast in the middle of 2004 with one child aboard. Two sons aboard now, one born in Auckland, a third child on the way, and a route behind them that has touched French Polynesia, New Zealand, Indonesia, Oman, Egypt and the Suez. He is thirty-three, and by that age has been an internet provider, a broker, a bank managing director in Madrid and a banker in Brazil. The family settles in Woodside, in the hills above Silicon Valley.
suggested_refs: simpaticasail.com/about-us

stops.name: Santiago, Vivendi buys the studio
stops.date_confidence: Attested: 'In February 2007, the studio was acquired by Vivendi Games for US$10 million', per the Wikipedia article on Behaviour Santiago, corroborated by contemporaneous coverage in Wired and GameSpot. Day unknown, set mid-month. Correction carried: the common shorthand that Activision bought Wanako is wrong, and so is the claim that the studio stayed inside Activision Blizzard. After the July 2008 Vivendi-Activision merger it was sold to Artificial Mind and Movement on 15 December 2008, renamed Behaviour Santiago in November 2010, and closed on 20 November 2017.
stops.campa: The month the boat reaches Miami, Vivendi Games buys Wanako for ten million dollars and files it under Sierra Online. The studio then changes hands the way small studios do: sold on to Artificial Mind and Movement in December 2008 after Vivendi merges with Activision, renamed Behaviour Santiago in November 2010, shut on the twentieth of November 2017, a decade after its founders had all gone. Biographies that say Activision bought Wanako are compressing four separate transactions into one, across a period in which Casares had no involvement at all.
suggested_refs: en.wikipedia.org, 'Behaviour Santiago'

segments.name: Palo Alto: the Tag, the Wallet, the Cafe

stops.name: Palo Alto, Bling Nation
stops.date_confidence: Attested to PayPal's 2016 DEF 14A, which dates his service as co-CEO of Bling Nation from March 2007 to October 2011. The US$20 million Series B led by Balderton Capital, part of roughly US$33 million raised in total, is attested to TechCrunch, 30 October 2009, and is folded into this stop. Palo Alto pin inherited byte-identical from reid_hoffman.journey.json.
stops.campa: The idea is a sticker. A small tag on the back of a phone, tapped against a reader at a corner shop, moving money between a community bank and a merchant without either of the card networks in the middle. Bling Nation raises about thirty-three million dollars, twenty of it from Balderton in October 2009, and signs up small banks in small towns. He runs it with Meyer Malka for four and a half years, from March 2007 to October 2011. It never reaches the number of shops and cardholders that a network of that shape needs to work.
suggested_refs: techcrunch.com/2009/10/30/bling-nation-raises-20-million-for-cell-phone-payment-system

stops.name: Pirque, the twenty-seventh of February
stops.date_confidence: The earthquake itself is public record: magnitude 8.8, central Chile, 27 February 2010. That it damaged the Las Majadas palace is reconstruction from Chilean press profiles; the direct fetch of lasmajadas.cl in the research pass did not mention the earthquake at all, and no engineering or insurance report was reached.
stops.campa: At 03:34 on a Saturday morning the ground under central Chile moves for three minutes at magnitude 8.8, one of the largest shocks ever instrumented anywhere. Old masonry does badly in such things. The 1905 house in the Maipo valley, four years into an ownership that has not yet decided what the house is for, is damaged; how badly is not stated in any document reached in this research, and the estate's own history page does not mention the earthquake at all. What is on record is that afterwards he considers selling.
suggested_refs: Chilean regional press profiles of Las Majadas (secondary)
sources: Public record of the 27 February 2010 Chile earthquake
Chilean press profiles of the Las Majadas restoration (tagged R)

stops.name: Palo Alto, Bosch says do not sell it
stops.date_confidence: Attested to lasmajadas.cl, fetched, which quotes Bosch directly on the conversation. The site gives no date for the visit; June 2010 orders it after the February earthquake. The same page gives the outcome: about US$30 million between the two partners across purchase, restoration and remodelling, opening commercially in 2015 with a hotel added in 2016.
stops.campa: Pablo Bosch, met years earlier in a Harvard classroom on the Allston side of the river, comes to Palo Alto and is told the Chilean house is going on the market. He argues the other way: not a residence, not a sale, but a damaged palace opened to strangers for the purpose of conversation, which he calls building social capital. It is an odd thing to say to a man who builds payment systems, and it works. The two of them will put some thirty million dollars into buying, restoring and remodelling the place. It opens commercially in 2015 and adds a hotel in 2016.
stops.quote: Wences me dijo que estaba pensando vender la propiedad, pero lo convenci de abrirla al encuentro y al dialogo.
stops.quote_source: Pablo Bosch, quoted at lasmajadas.cl (accents stripped for file encoding)
suggested_refs: lasmajadas.cl, 'La apuesta de Pablo Bosch y Wenceslao Casares en Las Majadas de Pirque'

stops.name: Palo Alto, Lemon Inc.

stops.campa: Lemon starts as an app that photographs receipts, which is a small enough idea that nobody objects to it. It becomes a wallet: cards, identification, loyalty numbers, a record of what was spent and where, carried in the phone instead of in a fold of leather. It is the third payments company in a row and the first one that will sell for money. He is running it and Bling Nation at the same time through most of 2011, the older company winding down while the newer one takes over its people.

stops.name: Palo Alto, two thousand dollars in cash at a cafe table
stops.date_confidence: Attested in his own telling, twice, from different interviews. The US$2,000 in cash and the QR code appear verbatim only in the Unchained transcript; the Craigslist seller, the Palo Alto cafe and the line quoted here appear in Bitcoin Magazine; EconTalk has the cafe and the transfer but neither the amount nor the reason. Flagged: the detail that the money was for repairing a bus comes from Reid Hoffman's retelling on Masters of Scale and is reconstruction, not in Casares's own accounts, which say only a common project with childhood friends. Month unknown.
stops.campa: He needs to send money to childhood friends in Argentina for something they are building together, and the ordinary channels will not do it. A friend says: try bitcoin. He finds a seller on Craigslist, meets him at a cafe in Palo Alto, hands over two thousand dollars in cash and receives, by a code scanned off a screen, two thousand dollars of something that then travels to Buenos Aires in minutes and is sold for pesos the next day. Reid Hoffman will retell this story with a seller who looks like Gandalf and a bus that needed repairs.
stops.quote: I felt like I was witnessing the beginning of the Internet.
stops.quote_source: Bitcoin Magazine, 'How The Man Who Introduced Silicon Valley To Bitcoin First Discovered It'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the whiskey bar and the handoff
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The meetup, the friend called Fede, the whiskey bar and the handing over of the group to a friend Diego, understood to be Diego Gutierrez Zaldivar, are attributed to Nathaniel Popper's Digital Gold (2015); no fetchable excerpt of Popper's text was reached in this pass and the detail is carried as widely repeated rather than verified. Month and venue are unknown; the city-centroid pin stands for an unnamed bar.
stops.campa: The first meetings are four or five people in a whiskey bar, organised with a friend called Fede, at a moment when the word bitcoin means nothing to anyone in the room next door. He hands the group over to another friend, Diego, and leaves it to grow. It grows: through 2013 the peso slides, exchange controls tighten, and a currency that no Argentine government can print becomes a subject people will cross the city to hear about. When Bitcoin Argentina is founded it names Diego Gutierrez Zaldivar, Rodolfo Andragnes and Franco Amati as its founders, and not him.

It is a year and a half into Lerner's work on bitcoin and he has not yet met anyone in it face to face.

segments.name: Xapo: the Vault and the Complaint

stops.name: Palo Alto, Xapo opens to the public
stops.date_confidence: Attested: PayPal's 2016 proxy dates his formal Xapo CEO tenure from March 2014, and contemporaneous venture coverage gives a first US$20 million round. Corrections carried: the round was led by Benchmark alongside Fortress Investment Group, Pantera Capital and Ribbit Capital, and Pantera had been dropped from the list that reached this file; and en.wikipedia dates the founding to late 2013, by Casares with COO Federico Murrone, with March 2014 the public opening rather than the founding.
stops.campa: Xapo is a wallet with a vault behind it: coins you spend held online, coins you keep held in cold storage the company will not put on a network at all. The premise is the one he has argued since the cafe table, that the asset's decisive property is not its price or its speed but that no one can stop a transfer. It is founded in late 2013 with Federico Murrone as chief operating officer, and opens to the public in March 2014 on twenty million dollars from Benchmark, Fortress, Pantera and Ribbit.
stops.quote: Bitcoin's most important quality is its censorship resistance, the rest will follow.
stops.quote_source: Wences Casares, Unchained podcast, Laura Shin interview, February 2018 (official unchainedcrypto.com transcript)

stops.name: Sun Valley, the first bitcoin given to Bill Gates
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction, and the least documented item in the file. Casares says he demonstrated bitcoin to Bill Gates and gave him his first bitcoin, in the context of the Allen and Company conference at Sun Valley; the quantity, the year and Gates's subsequent disposition of it are established nowhere. The Forbes Argentina piece usually cited for it returned a 404 on fetch. The Allen and Company conference runs in early or mid July, which fixes the month and not the year. Nothing in this stop is confirmed beyond his own retelling.
stops.campa: Once a year a merchant bank gathers the owners of American media and technology in a ski resort in Idaho, and by his account he speaks there in a slot before the Bezos and Buffett conversation and afterwards meets Bill Gates in a hallway. He explains bitcoin. He gives Gates his first bitcoin. Reid Hoffman, watching him do this to room after room, will call him bitcoin's Patient Zero, a label that writes the miners and the exchanges already running out of the story. How much he gave, in what year, and what became of it, no source says, and the article most often cited for the whole scene is gone from the web.

Lemon and Lemon Argentina sued Casares, Cynthia McAdam, Federico Murrone, Martin Apesteguia and Fabian Cuesta in Santa Clara County, alleging Xapo was developed using Lemon and LifeLock facilities, computers and resources while its founders were still employed there, and alleging breach of employment and fiduciary duties. The complaint filed in Santa Clara County names Casares and four former Lemon employees, among them Federico Murrone, and alleges that Xapo was built inside LifeLock's walls on LifeLock's machines while its founders were drawing LifeLock salaries. The claims are breach of employment terms and breach of fiduciary duty. They are allegations. No court reached in this research has ruled on their merits.

stops.name: Attinghausen, the mountain
stops.date_confidence: Attested as to the facility and its use: a decommissioned Swiss military installation of 1947, dug more than 320 metres into granite near Attinghausen in the canton of Uri, repurposed by Xapo from 2014 for offline key storage, reported by the World Economic Forum, CBC Radio and Bitcoinist. Two coordinates for Attinghausen had reached this file, 46.8747/8.6247 and 46.8536/8.6156; the second is within roughly 500 metres of the village and is used here for both. Month unknown. The US$10 billion figure is an informed estimate from client interviews, never an audited disclosure.
stops.campa: The vault is a hole in a mountain. A Swiss army bunker of 1947, driven three hundred and twenty metres into granite in the canton of Uri, fitted with computers that never touch a network, biometric doors, mantraps, multiple signatures required to move anything, and a deliberate delay between a customer asking for coins and the transaction being signed. Nothing is buried there. What the granite protects is key material and the procedure for using it; the coins sit where they have always sat, on a ledger anyone can read. Reporters are told it holds ten billion dollars in bitcoin, a figure from client interviews that no audit confirms.
stops.quote: Nobody controls Bitcoin. Not Russ, not any one person, not any group of people, not any one company, not one country.
stops.quote_source: Wences Casares, EconTalk, interview by Russ Roberts, 20 July 2015
suggested_refs: World Economic Forum, 'This former military bunker in the Swiss mountains is keeping Bitcoin safe'

stops.name: San Jose, the cross-complaint and the letter
stops.date_confidence: Attested as allegation and pleading. Fortune of 28 July 2015 reports Casares's cross-claims for breach of contract, conversion and unjust enrichment, and a February 2014 letter from LifeLock president Hilary Schneider stating that LifeLock recognised his bitcoin work as unrelated to its business. A California court later stayed the action on an inconvenient-forum motion and related litigation went to Delaware; CoinDesk reports a further suit filed 22 September 2016. stops.campa: He files back. Breach of contract, conversion, unjust enrichment, and one document: a letter from LifeLock's own president, dated February 2014, saying the company understood his bitcoin work to be unrelated to its business. The California action is later stayed on a forum motion and the fight moves to Delaware; a further suit is filed against him in September 2016. What no reachable record shows is an ending. No merits verdict has been published, and if there was a settlement it was not made public.

stops.name: Geneva, one of five directors
stops.date_confidence: Date attested: the first Libra Association council meeting was held on 14 October 2019, and the withdrawal sequence is documented, PayPal on 4 October, eBay, Mastercard, Stripe, Visa and Mercado Pago on 11 October, Booking Holdings on the 14th. stops.campa: Facebook proposes a global currency and assembles two dozen companies behind it. Within ten days the payment networks leave: PayPal first, then eBay, Mastercard, Stripe, Visa and Mercado Pago together, then Booking Holdings on the morning of the council meeting itself. Of the members still standing, five are elected directors, and one of them is Casares, representing Xapo. In December 2020 Libra is renamed Diem and cut down to something much smaller. In January 2022 the assets are sold to Silvergate Capital for a reported two hundred million dollars and nothing launches.

stops.name: Gibraltar, the bank licensed
stops.date_confidence: Attested to Xapo Bank's own corporate history at xapobank.com and to the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission's bank register. The company dates the birth of the licensed bank to 2021 and gives no month, so the day defaults. The structural point, that fiat deposits fall under Gibraltar's statutory deposit protection while bitcoin custody is governed by segregation and custody law and not by deposit insurance, is drawn from the company's own compliance pages.
stops.campa: The custody company becomes a bank. Xapo Bank Limited is licensed as a credit institution in Gibraltar, which means the dollars a customer holds sit inside a statutory deposit-protection scheme and the bitcoin does not: the coins are protected instead by segregation and custody law, which is a different promise made by different lawyers. Seamus Rocca, chief executive since 2017, runs it. Casares is founder and executive chairman and no longer runs anything day to day.

The thing his mother could not do with two plastic bags of cash in a supermarket aisle in 1989, hold value overnight, is now a licensed service with a compliance department.
